page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage or GPUs, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 67 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the server's exceptional memory subsystem performance. It achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, recording 427.21 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 200.77 GB/sec for large-block write operations. The Passmark memory score and database operations both rank in the top 10%, with database operations reaching 47851.85. Multi-core processing is also highly efficient, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21725.0, placing it in the top 10%. Redis SET operations perform strongly at 67.66 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 74.31 GB/sec. However, text generation for small LLM models is a relative bottleneck, registering a lower-tier speed of 26.03 tokens per second.

The r8gb.8xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications due to its dedicated ARMv9 cores and dense memory allocation, which minimizes resource contention without the overhead of hyperthreading. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized choice for workloads that rely heavily on RAM and network-attached storage. This server is highly suited for in-memory databases like Redis, high-throughput database operations, memory-intensive web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
